keywords: how do anti theft tags work

scenes.visual: close-up illustration of a hard white plastic anti-theft tag clipped to the hem of a folded blue shirt on a clothes shop table, a small round grey pin dome on one end of the tag, the tag and shirt in the lower two-thirds of the frame, simple soft shop background
scenes.narration: That hard plastic tag on a new shirt... how does the shop door *know*?

scenes.visual: illustration of two tall pale grey security gate panels standing at the entrance of an Indian clothes shop, a young Indian woman with a shopping bag walking out between them and glancing at them curiously, seen from inside the shop, the gates and the woman in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: First, yesterday's green dot? B, camera or mic. Now this tag... stick around, the till trick is *better*.
scenes.headline: HOW DOES IT *KNOW*?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the tag turns see-through and shows a thin metal strip inside; a battery icon gets a red cross
scenes.narration: Okay, so. Inside? No battery, no camera. Mostly just a thin *metal* strip. So what's it for?
scenes.headline: NO *BATTERY*

scenes.visual: illustration of a silver tuning fork held upright by one hand above a wooden table, soft curved sound lines spreading out from its two prongs, plain cream background, the fork in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Here's the weird part. The gates *ping* it... and the strip *rings*, like a tuning fork.
scenes.headline: IT *RINGS*?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: a gate panel sends pulses, the strip in the tag wobbles, a counter climbs to 58,000 times a second, then the gate goes quiet and the strip keeps ringing back
scenes.narration: About *fifty-eight thousand* times a second. And it keeps ringing after the gate goes *quiet*. Why?
scenes.headline: *58,000* A SECOND

scenes.visual: illustration of the two pale grey security gate panels at a clothes shop door glowing softly, a small red alarm light lit on top of one panel, a paper shopping bag with a folded blue shirt passing between them, seen from the side, the gates in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Because in that silence, the gates *listen*. <short pause> Hear a ring... beep. They're not watching you. They're *listening*.
scenes.headline: THEY *LISTEN*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: cross-section of the tag on a shirt, a magnet under the counter glows, the little clamp inside pulls apart and the tag lifts free of the pin
scenes.narration: So how does the cashier *unlock* it? A strong *magnet* in the counter pulls the lock open. Click.
scenes.headline: THE TILL *TRICK*

scenes.visual: illustration of a folded white shirt lying on a shop counter with a broken round plastic tag on it and a big blue ink stain spreading across the fabric, seen from above at a slight angle, simple counter background, the shirt in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Some hide *ink*, so forcing one off ruins the shirt. Next time a gate beeps, you'll know it heard a ring.
scenes.headline: THE *INK* TRAP

scenes.narration: These legends got it first. Nicely done!
scenes.narration_none: Nobody cracked yesterday's one... <chuckles> let's see if you can beat today's.
scenes.headline: *SHOUTOUT*

scenes.narration: Tomorrow's teaser: tap-to-pay cards. A, hidden battery? B, the machine powers it? Comment your guess.

youtube.title: How do anti theft tags work? #shorts
youtube.description:
How do anti theft tags work? Many of those hard security tags on clothes have no battery, just a thin metal strip. The shop security gates ping it with quick bursts, the strip rings back like a tuning fork (about 58,000 times a second), and the gates listen for that ring in the quiet gaps. At the till, a strong magnet unlocks the tag. Some tags also hide ink vials that ruin the item if forced off.
